post_text: Went out yesterday, shoreline ice was heaved upward but still accessible. Ice was in good shape 8-10” with zero snow…small puddles here and there. Caught some perch but zero walleye. I was marking them but very lazy and none would commit

post_text: There was 5-6” ice to the east of huffs where we were today. Marked a few good ones but they just cruised on by. Got one little walleye and that was it.
review_note: First-person same-day report explicitly says one small walleye.

post_text: Fished it this weekend. Everywhere I seen was about 4-5 inches with 2 inches of white ice on top. Fishing was very slow didn’t see any walleye just caught a couple small perch Lots of huts out there but it seemed everyone I talked to had tough luck there too

post_text: Well we fished the channel west of North Port in 16 ft of water . We took home 4 walleyes ranging 3-4 lbs and missed what to be a 5lber at the hole . Heading out again this morning. Tight lines everyone !

post_text: Hi Turk, I’ve never spent much time evening fishing. By the time I get home put everything away it’s pretty late. Yesterday I started at 9:00 am and fished all day. A couple of Sheepshead and that was it. Didn’t have anything happening the next day so I thought I’d stay out and see what happens. 5:00 pm the fish started biting and by 7:00 pm I had my limit. Was a beautiful evening and we’ll worth the wait. Next trip I think I’ll start later in the day. Thanks 1000002962 1000002962 1920×1268 932 KB
